For a 5-year horizon, I suggest the existing bond composition remains suitable. However, I'll re-evaluate the maturities to enhance the laddered structure. Our options for near maturity are limited, but we can consider a slightly shorter-term bond to maintain a balance without crossing the 7-year mark. A mix of 10-year and 15-year bonds will provide stable returns while maintaining the 'no more than 30%' threshold in any single year. Upon analysis, I recommend a 60:40 split between 10-year and 15-year maturities to keep the portfolio diversified. This allocation allows us to maintain the optimal credit quality and spread the maturity risk. Our current bonds will be adjusted to include the recently issued 10-year bond with a BBB rating and the 15-year bond with an A rating. These bonds should remain within our investment-grade parameters and duration limits.
